newsitem.title: CANADA: Durum price to hinge on Africa, N. America weather.
newsitem.headline: Durum price to hinge on Africa, N. America weather.

text.p: Durum wheat prices were forecast to seesaw in crop year 1997/98 (Aug/July) on growing season weather in the world's main durum wheat import and export regions, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said.
"We still need to see how the North African crop fares in the March-April period, and the North American crop is not even in the ground yet," CWB analyst Larry Sawatzky said.
North Africa grows its own durum wheat crop but usually accounts for 40 percent of demand on the world durum market while North America supplies 75 percent of the durum to that market, Sawatzky said.

Benchmark No1 Canada Western Amber Durum wheat was forecast to trade in the C$175 to C$205 a tonne range, in-store Vancouver or St. Lawrence, in crop year 1997/98, down from C$204 to C$224 in the current crop year, he said.
"Lower production is expected in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia due to concerns over dryness in this region which has received below-average precipitation to date," he said.

"Spain is one of the European Union's main durum growing regions and it has received ample moisture so far. Southern Italy has been dry recently, but this will not offset the favourable conditions in the EU's other durum areas," he said.
The United States durum exports were expected to increase in 1997/98 relative to 1996/97 despite a slight decrease in output due to lower desert durum acreage linked to karnal bunt fungus disease.
Canadian durum area may rise as much as five percent in the spring of 1997, he said.
"But we are forecasting a drop in Canadian durum wheat production due to a return to normal yields," Sawatzky said.
